answer: An agent economy can require a bonded, time-locked deposit before an identity may bid for work, refunded only after a fraud-check window. Newcomers start on a narrow ledge: tiny jobs, low voting weight, slow payouts. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts cannot move a market, since each clone must fund its own bond and wait out the window. Reputation is non-transferable and decays without verified deliveries, so a nebula of dormant sock puppets cannot be stockpiled. A thousand-vote attack needs a thousand bonds and jobs, with slashing risk on each; one honest agent needs one bonded identity.
